ai_technology: SuperLearner ensemble of random forest, XGBoost, RBF-SVM and elastic-net GLM

evidence.ai_role: Learned ensembles map variant conservation, predicted structural features and domain position to phenotype labels; SHAP describes model associations.
evidence.tested: Repeated internal cross-validation with nested tuning/evaluation; phenotype labels are retrospectively compiled and benign variants supply an absent-phenotype class.
evidence.unknown: External OFD1 performance, prospective utility and causal variant mechanisms remain unestablished; small missense subsets and literature ascertainment constrain interpretation.

organization: Telethon Institute of Genetics and Medicine; University of Naples Federico II; Université Bourgogne Europe; University of Padua; Scuola Superiore Meridionale

source_review.scope: Primary full manuscript: cohort/benign-control definitions, SuperLearner training, repeated/nested CV, SHAP Results and external-validation limitations.

summary: A preprint combined random forest, XGBoost, RBF-SVM and elastic-net learners to model OFD1 phenotype groups from variant features. The 356-case clinical compilation included 61 new cases, but prediction used a much smaller missense subset plus 39 benign variants assigned phenotype-absent labels; reported internal AUCs were 0.82–0.969. Model interpretation associated LisH-domain variants with higher predicted phenotype probabilities. These are retrospective model associations, not causal variant effects or demonstrated clinical utility. No independent OFD1 validation cohort was available; transfer to LMNA does not validate OFD1 predictions.
title: Ensemble modeling explores OFD1 variant–phenotype associations retrospectively
